decision: Wrote .shilaycow/pitfalls.md from the system-design Retro comment: five entries, each with count 1
why: The owner left no comments on the finished tracking issue, so the Retro is the only source

decision: Found that no container image can be built in the agent environment (no Docker daemon); asked the owner how S-12 should be proven and carried on with everything else
why: S-12 says the image is built and started; pretending to prove it another way would change an approved scenario
evidence: needs-owner issue; docker info output in the tracking issue

decision: Dropped SESSION_SECRET from the settings
why: Both the session token and the anti-forgery token are random values stored server-side, so nothing is signed; one less key to keep. The system design's settings table is corrected in this task

decision: The sign-in group is optional at the server; an unrecognised group is INVALID with 「請選擇類型」
why: Appendix B says the group is not required and the interface always sends it; IAM-R03's scenarios sign in by name alone. v2's string is used for the unrecognised value

decision: A failed sign-in commits its failure count even though the request is refused
why: The count must survive the refusal; this is the one deliberate exception to "a refusal rolls everything back", written down in the design

decision: A sign-in attempt refused as RATE_LIMITED is not itself recorded
why: Otherwise a client that keeps retrying would stay limited forever; the spec says 10 attempts are evaluated per minute

decision: An unauthenticated browser page request gets status 401 with the sign-in page as its body, not a redirect
why: The spec binds UNAUTHENTICATED to 401; the person still lands on the sign-in page

decision: Each test gets a database copied from a migrated template instead of truncating tables
why: The audit table refuses TRUNCATE, concurrency tests need real connections, and v3's per-test truncation was slow

decision: Two health pages: /health public with no detail, /status for administrators
why: Whether storage and the key are configured should not be visible to visitors

decision: Browser smoke test uses the Node Playwright already installed, driven from pytest, and is skipped with a printed reason when unavailable unless REQUIRE_BROWSER=1
why: Installing another Playwright would not find the installed browser; CI sets the variable so absence is a failure there

decision: Cut the build into five tickets in a chain, T-03 and T-04 in parallel, each verified before merging
why: Care level 謹慎; 11 of 16 sessions planned, 5 left for fix rounds

decision: Extended tools/check_spec.py to compare every written count under docs/ with the feature files, and removed the per-task count columns and totals row from the task map
why: Finding 2 of the system-design verdict and pitfall 2: fewer copies of a number, and each remaining copy is checked. Seen to fail for the index sentence, an area row, a feature row and a split feature's rows

decision: Restored three lines of v3's front page into docs/spec/index.md (source, readers, the "who owns the data" sentence) and listed every remaining wording difference from a line-by-line comparison
why: Finding 1 and pitfall 1: the list is now produced from a diff, with the command in the document

decision: Added six message strings to appendix B and set the message for an unrecognised sign-in group
why: The owner approved v2's strings in the brief (assumption 2)

decision: Split AUD-F01 between task 2 (AUD-R01) and task 8 (AUD-R02, AUD-R03) in the task map and the audit area index
why: The owner approved it in the brief (assumption 1)

decision: Edited documents of the finished system-design task (design sections 9.2, 9.3, 9.7; open questions; task map; difference list)
why: They are the living design the later tasks read; brief S-14 asks for these corrections

decision: Updated the design after T-01: the HTTP status is Outcome.status, any response of 400 or above rolls back, the actor is carried in request.state.actor, and migration numbers must follow merge order
why: T-01 found CONFLICT and BLOCKED share 409, which an enum value cannot express; the other three are interface facts T-02 to T-04 build on

decision: Outcome carries its HTTP status as outcome.status, not as the enum value the design shows
why: CONFLICT and BLOCKED are both 409; Python merges enum members with equal values, so BLOCKED would report itself as CONFLICT

decision: The request transaction is an ASGI middleware that commits when the response status is below 400 and rolls back otherwise, decided before the response starts
why: A FastAPI dependency with yield finishes at a point that has moved between FastAPI versions; the middleware does not depend on it. Any 4xx or 5xx rolls back, not only a Refusal

decision: The error handler takes the signed-in person from request.state.actor
why: T-01 has no sessions; the handler needs one agreed place to find the actor when it writes ACCESS_DENIED

decision: The ACCESS_DENIED description is the refusal message, a colon and the attempted action; without an attempted action it is the method and path
why: The design says only that the description contains the action

decision: The refusal page is a built-in HTML string, with no template engine yet
why: Templates belong to T-02; adding Jinja here would be a dependency nothing in this ticket uses

decision: migrate also refuses an applied file that is missing and a pending file older than one already applied
why: Forward only: a database that skipped a file has a different history from one that did not. Two tickets adding migrations in parallel must number them in merge order

decision: The migration runner takes the clock and writes applied_at itself; the time scan also covers migrations/
why: The design forbids database time functions; the same rule is applied to the runner and the SQL files

decision: Migrations are found at the repository root next to the app package, not packaged inside it
why: The design puts migrations/ at the root; this works for an editable install and for an image that copies the repository, not for a wheel

decision: One statement-level trigger refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on audit_log; no check constraint on the type column
why: Statement level also refuses statements that match no row. The type list lives in appendix C and the code constants; a third copy in SQL would be one more place to drift

decision: audit_log.actor_account_id has no foreign key yet
why: The accounts table arrives in T-02, which can add the key in its migration

decision: serve takes --host and --port (default 127.0.0.1:8000) as arguments, and turns off uvicorn's own proxy-header handling
why: Host and port are not in the design's settings table and only settings are read from the environment; the client address must be worked out in one place from TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS

decision: /health waits at most 2 seconds for a connection, and the app starts even when the database is down
why: So /health can answer 503 instead of the process hanging or dying; serve still fails earlier if the migration cannot connect

decision: An unknown path keeps the framework's default 404 body
why: The ticket asks for 404 and no write; a styled page belongs with the templates

decision: The test dependency is httpx2, not httpx
why: The installed Starlette test client warns that httpx is deprecated in favour of httpx2

decision: Tests were written after the code and each behaviour proven by breaking it; three safeguards are kept without a failing test
why: 74 single breaks, 72 caught; the rest are named under Not proven in the Ready comment

decision: Merged T-01 after an independent PASS at 2e5c8e8; its five findings go into T-02 (findings 1, 2, 3, 5) and T-05 (finding 4) as numbered behaviours to prove
why: Care level 謹慎; small fixes ride with the next tickets instead of costing a builder and a verifier of their own
evidence: pull request 8 verdict; tickets T-02 and T-05

decision: Counted the time budget as active time: a usage limit stopped every session from about 00:31Z to 02:10Z and that pause is not counted
why: The budget limits what the task spends; nothing ran during the pause. Wall-clock time since the start is reported beside it so the owner can count differently

decision: S-12's container image is proven by a CI job that builds and boots it (issue 7, option A); the owner adds the workflow file to the task branch
why: Chosen by the owner in conversation; the agent environment has no Docker daemon

decision: The time budget counts active working time, not pauses caused by a usage limit
why: Confirmed by the owner in conversation

decision: Changed two files outside the ticket's Touches list: app/main.py (static files, password hasher) and app/core/outcomes.py (install(app, page): the refusal page comes from templates)
why: Templates and static files cannot be served without the app factory, and T-01 left the built-in refusal page for T-02 to replace; nothing else builds in parallel with T-02

decision: Every refusal of a request that wants HTML with outcome UNAUTHENTICATED shows the sign-in page, not only GET as design section 5 says
why: A wrong password is a POST and the person should see the form again with the message; the design needs this line updated

decision: app/core/web.py imports app.accounts.service to resolve the session
why: The design puts "who is signed in" in core/web.py and sessions in accounts; one inward import is simpler than a registration hook

decision: Step definitions under tests/steps are found automatically and are visible to the features of every area; two tests guard against one text matching two definitions
why: pytest-bdd picks one silently; later tasks add step modules without editing tests/test_spec.py

decision: The spec's tags (@IAM-F01, @money, @concurrency ...) are not turned into pytest marks
why: Most contain a hyphen and cannot be selected with -m; as marks they only produce unknown-mark warnings. Selecting by rule is done by the implemented list

decision: the name list is exactly compares the names in order (name order), not as a set
why: The examples are written in name order and a stable order is what a person expects from a picker

decision: The IAM-R03 step signs in without a group; an empty or unrecognised group value is INVALID, only an absent field is "left out"
why: With a group, appendix B refuses a name that is not on its list as INVALID before the password is looked at, which would hide what IAM-R03 is about

decision: a visitor requests any protected action requests every route the application describes except a public list kept in the test
why: Routes added by later tasks are covered without anyone remembering; a new public route has to be added to the list on purpose

decision: The shared background is applied by the world fixture from background.md; its "defaults in Appendix A" step loads nothing yet, and an unknown background step fails the scenario
why: Nothing stores prices or retention before the settings task; failing on an unknown step keeps a change to the background from being ignored

decision: Background accounts are created through accounts.service.create_account; the archived one is marked by SQL
why: No action archives an account before Task 4

decision: CLOCK_OFFSET_MINUTES must be within plus or minus 527040 (366 days)
why: Too large to apply needs a limit; a year is more than trying a timeout by hand needs

decision: Any error raised while migrating, including a database that cannot be reached, is reported as "migration 失敗"; a database error anywhere else in a command is "資料庫錯誤"
why: The finding was that unrelated errors would be mislabelled; the migration is still what failed when it cannot connect

decision: The time scan forbids .now( on anything not named clock, .today( on anything, and "from time import"
why: An alias can be any name, so the scan looks at the call rather than the import

decision: The session cookie is set HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ already; Secure in production is left to T-03
why: A cookie without them would be a regression waiting for T-03; Secure depends on APP_ENV, which T-03 owns

decision: audit_log.actor_account_id still has no foreign key to accounts
why: Design section 8 shows none, and T-01's tests write audit rows for actors that are not accounts

decision: The role shown for OWNER is 擁有者 (ADMIN 管理員, USER 員工)
why: The spec names the other two; 擁有者 is the word the earlier documents use once

decision: htmx 2.0.4 is vendored from the npm package htmx.org; the integrity attribute is computed from the served file and a test pins it to the published value
why: Fixed version with a hash, as the design asks; one source for the hash

decision: The sign-in page needs JavaScript: the name list is filled by htmx when a group is chosen
why: The design's /sign-in/names fragment; a no-script fallback was not asked for

decision: gherkin-official is pinned to 43.0.0 in the dev dependencies, the version tools/requirements.txt pins
why: The runner's count is compared with the check tool's; both should read the files with the same parser

decision: Tests were written after the code except for behaviours 11, 13 and 14; 102 single breaks, 101 caught, the other named under Not proven
why: Same method as T-01

decision: Merged T-02 after an independent PASS at 8300c39; findings 2 and 4 go into T-03, findings 1 and 3 into T-04, finding 5 and 7 into the design as written; finding 6 (the time scan is stricter than needed) is left as it is
why: Same reasoning as T-01: small fixes ride with the next tickets. An over-strict scan fails loudly and costs only a rename
evidence: pull request 9 verdict; tickets T-03 and T-04; design sections 4, 5, 8, 11.3

decision: The session is resolved (idle window restarted, or ended on timeout) in a transaction of its own, committed whatever becomes of the request
why: Inside the request's transaction a refusal rolled the timeout back, so a timed-out session came back to life when the clock was set back; and a person whose requests were refused for 30 minutes would have been signed out while using the system

decision: The session is resolved and the anti-forgery token checked by one dependency on the whole application (web.guard_session), before every route
why: One place, and routes added by later tasks are covered without anyone remembering; resolving before the route takes its connection means no request holds one connection while waiting for another. Requests with no route (404, static files) do not resolve the session

decision: POST /sign-in needs no anti-forgery token even when the browser still holds a live session
why: The design says sign-in is not checked; a sign-in page left open in another tab has no token to send, and refusing it would also write ACCESS_DENIED against the person. It is the only exception, in web._NO_TOKEN_NEEDED

decision: The token is accepted only from the X-CSRF-Token header or the csrf_token form field (urlencoded or multipart), not from the query or a JSON body
why: What the design names; a token in a URL ends up in logs and history

decision: Sign-out answers with a redirect to /sign-in?signed-out, and the sign-in page shows 「您已登出」 at that address as role="status"
why: Reloading the page after signing out does not send the POST again; the notice is not a refusal so it is not an alert. Anyone can open that address and see the notice, which says nothing about anyone

decision: Sign-out ends only the session it came from; the person's other sessions stay
why: Design 9.3: sessions of one person are independent

decision: The scenario "Saved data survives a timeout" runs without saving a report: it checks that a timeout removes and changes no stored row, and its Given step fails once a table named like a report exists
why: Reports are built by a later task and the ticket asks for all 8 scenarios to run; a stand-in report would prove nothing. The guard makes the later task finish the step instead of relying on a note

decision: world.send now carries the session's anti-forgery token on every request of a signed-in actor that is not GET or HEAD; csrf=False leaves it out. world.sign_in reads the token from the landing page. Added world.signed_in and world.csrf_token
why: Every later state-changing step would otherwise have to remember the token; this is what the shared layout does for a real page. An addition to the common interface, written in its README

decision: <name> signs in, "… signs in again" and "… signs in with the correct password" are one step definition
why: They mean the same request; one definition cannot drift from another

decision: <name> requests a protected action requests the landing page of that person's role
why: The only protected thing every role may do in this task

decision: pytest-bdd pinned to ==9.0.1, and a test fails when the installed version is not the pinned one
why: T-02 verdict finding 4; the test stops an environment with another version from running the harness unnoticed

decision: Tests written after the code; 50 single breaks, 49 caught, the other (a rule removed from implemented_rules.txt is skipped, as designed) named under Not proven
why: Same method as T-01 and T-02

decision: Merged T-03 after an independent PASS at 33a2b80; its seven findings are not fixed in this task: finding 1 is work for the reports task, findings 4 and 6 are notes for later tasks, findings 5 and 7 are left for the owner, findings 2 and 3 are about the Ready comment
why: None affects a scenario of this task; T-05 is already the largest ticket

decision: A sign-in form refused as INVALID (no name, name not on the group's list, unknown group, NUL byte) is not recorded as an attempt and does not count toward the address's limit
why: The ticket says such a refusal writes nothing, and the existing tests say the same; design 9.2 step 1 could be read as recording every attempt that is not limited. Only refusals that reach an account or a password commit

decision: Rows of sign_in_attempts are never deleted
why: Nothing in the ticket or the design asks for pruning; left out as the smallest change. The table grows by one row per evaluated attempt and will need a clean-up later

decision: An attempt exactly 60 seconds old no longer counts toward the limit
why: Same reading as the lock (15 min 00 s is over) and the session timeout

decision: A NUL byte in the password is a wrong password (UNAUTHENTICATED), not INVALID; in the group it is INVALID 請選擇類型; only in the name is it INVALID 請選擇帳戶
why: The ticket says "the same holds for any other text field"; I read that as "never a 500". The password never reaches the database and the group is checked against the list in Python, so each keeps its existing rule

decision: With TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=n and fewer than n values in X-Forwarded-For, the address is the connection's peer
why: The design does not say; the peer is the only address nobody could have made up

decision: An attempt refused as LOCKED still counts toward the address's limit, though not toward the account's failures
why: It is an attempt from that address; the brief's assumption 8 only excludes it from the failure count and the lock

decision: The sign-in groups live in app/accounts/service.py as GROUPS (label, roles, zone); the store takes roles and zone as parameters instead of holding SQL per group
why: One owner for the list; the picker and both checks read it

decision: Changed two existing tests of tests/unit/test_sign_in.py: a missing password now writes the failure count and an attempt row, and the session test looks only at the sessions table
why: Both asserted that sign-in writes nothing else, which this ticket deliberately ends

decision: Simultaneous requests in tests are made certain by holding a table lock until every connection is waiting, not by starting threads together and hoping
why: The ticket asks that the scenario fail every time without the guard; a race left to timing fails only sometimes
evidence: tests/support/together.py; 20 of 20 failures without each guard

decision: Added World.prepare for requests a Given sends, and the steps read failed_count and locked_until from the accounts table for "the failure count is" and "is not locked"
why: The scenes are built through the real POST /sign-in; the count has no page that shows it, and the design names those columns

decision: store.credentials_of was renamed credentials_for_sign_in because it now locks the account's row
why: The old name hid the lock; T-03 will meet a conflict here if it calls the old name

decision: Merged T-04 after an independent PASS at 54ddada, resolving four conflicts with T-03 and changing one T-03 test to expect the attempt row T-04 adds
why: Each ticket was right alone; together a sign-in writes a session and an attempt. Full suite on the merged branch: 357 passed, 472 skipped. This merge commit was not judged by a ticket verifier; the final verification covers it
evidence: merge commit of T-04 on task/skeleton-and-sign-in; tests/unit/test_sessions.py

decision: T-04's findings 2 and 3 go into T-05 as behaviours to prove; findings 4 and 5 are left as they are; finding 1 is about the Ready comment
why: A 500 from an over-long forwarded address is a defect worth fixing now; the repeated "15 minutes" follows from the rule that messages are literal strings

decision: Folded the built rules into docs/spec: IAM-F01 to F03 and AUD-R01 moved up to 情境 in their area indexes, and the limits decided while building listed under 規則
why: The spec must say what is true when the pull request is merged; written while T-05 runs because T-05 adds no spec rule. The command rule will be checked against what T-05 delivers before the pull request

decision: create-owner gives the owner the zone WEST without asking
why: Every account must have a zone (migration 0002) and the design says the command asks only for a name and a password; nothing reads the owner's zone

decision: create-owner applies appendix B's password length (6 to 30) and writes one ACCOUNT_CREATE audit row with actor SYSTEM
why: The ticket speaks of an audit row but not of who the actor is; no person is signed in at a terminal

decision: seed-demo is refused when any account exists, writes no audit rows, and uses one public password (demo-password) printed by the command
why: A second run would collide on names and on the single owner; demo data is not an action of anyone

decision: The nine demo accounts are written out in app/accounts/demo.py and a test compares them with docs/spec/background.md
why: The image does not contain docs/, so the program cannot parse the spec at run time; pitfall 2 asks that a copy be checked by a tool

decision: A forwarded value that is not an IP address (or is longer than 45 characters) is ignored and the request is counted under its peer; an accepted address is stored in its canonical form
why: A trusted proxy writes only addresses, so anything else did not come from one; the alternative, truncating the text, would let a client choose its own bucket

decision: The image installs the program in place (pip install -e .) and reads the port from PORT in the CMD line, not in the program
why: One copy of the code with migrations/ beside it, the same layout the tests run; the design says nothing but config.py reads the environment, and --port already exists

decision: migrate (and so serve) fails when the migrations directory holds no files
why: The ticket's note: starting on an empty schema would look like a working system

decision: /status always shows the database as 可連線 and has no branch for an unreachable database
why: The page is only reached after the session was read from the database; /health is what reports an unreachable database

decision: test_command is "python -m pytest" without REQUIRE_BROWSER=1
why: The design has the browser test skip where Node or Playwright is missing and CI set REQUIRE_BROWSER=1; putting it in test_command would fail on a machine without Playwright

decision: The browser test and the try-it skill find Playwright through NODE_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, defaulting to this environment's /opt paths when they exist
why: Node's Playwright is not a dependency this repository installs; the workflow file installs playwright 1.63.0 (the version here) and sets NODE_PATH

decision: The container image is not proven: it was never built
why: No Docker daemon here (issue 7); only the start sequence and a static reading of the Dockerfile are tested

decision: Merged T-05 after an independent PASS at 7f6a2a8; its six findings are not fixed in this task and are listed in the report for the owner
why: None affects a scenario; the browser test's weakness (finding 1) is covered by the spec scenarios for landing by role

decision: Changed the CI workflow file to also run on pushes to task/** branches
why: The workflow ran only on pull requests and on main; S-12's image job must run before the pull request into main is opened, and a task's work is then checked before its pull request exists. Changed after T-05's verdict; the final verification covers it

decision: Added .github/workflows/ci.yml to the task branch (commit 504cbd5), identical to the prepared file
why: Issue 7, option A; workflow files are the owner's to add

decision: Took S-12 as met on the CI run of commit 504cbd5: test, spec and image jobs all succeeded on the first run
why: The image job built the image, checked it does not run as root, saw it refuse to start without DATABASE_URL, and saw /health answer 200 with production settings

decision: Fix round after the final verdict FAIL at 4fc0563 (S-14): the spec check now covers totals stated in sentences of living documents and the count of built rules against tests/implemented_rules.txt; the system design, task map and this task's design no longer repeat the totals
why: The verdict showed 137 written where nothing checked it, one place added by this task, and that removing a built rule from the list failed nothing. Seen to fail eight ways after the fix; full suite 389 passed

decision: The Chief made this fix itself instead of starting a builder
why: The failed work was the Chief's own (S-14); a builder would cost a session and add nothing. A fresh session judges the new head

decision: Records of a moment (each task's brief.md and reports/, spec-baseline-diff.md) are deliberately not checked for totals
why: They state what was true when written and must not be edited when the spec grows; the rule is written in docs/spec/conventions.md and named in the report for the owner to overrule

decision: Did not fix the verdict's other findings in this round (old session left open on a second sign-in, TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS default, CI running twice per commit, English 404 body) except the empty headings in the accounts index
why: They are behaviour or owner-file changes that would need tests and a wider re-check; the fix round changes no program behaviour
